assays.assay_description: Mice received i.p. psilocin or mushroom extract (0.25-2 mg/kg) and head-twitches were counted (observation after 10 min). In a separate experiment, hallucinogen (1 mg/kg) was given 15 min before 5-HTP (200 mg/kg, i.p.) and HTR was counted over 10 and 20 min.

outcomes.summary: Psilocin and both mushroom extracts elicited dose-dependent head-twitch responses in female mice, with 1 mg/kg producing maximal HTR; higher doses (2 mg/kg) reduced HTR. Pre-treatment with 1 mg/kg hallucinogen reduced 5-HTP (200 mg/kg)-induced HTR by ~60% (psilocin) and ~30-46% (extracts), consistent with partial agonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors.
outcomes.statistics: one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc; * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001 vs. control
outcomes.evidence: Dose of 1 mg/kg elicited the maximal number of head twitches in mice. Further increasing of the amounts of hallucinogens decreased the number of observed head twitches... The application of pure psilocin gave significantly lower head-twitch response (about 60% lower) compared to the effect of full agonist (5-HTP)

judge_notes: Acute toxicity (LD50) experiments were excluded — lethality is a physiological/mortality endpoint, not a behavioural assay (the paper mentions behavioural disturbance only qualitatively).
Dose-response HTR and 5-HTP-potentiation HTR collapsed into a single HTR assay per rubric (same paradigm, different pharmacological manipulations).

D2 scored 0 (<15 min) — primary dose-response observation was 10 min; the 20-min observation in the 5-HTP arm is borderline but the 'longest single session' was 20 min only in part of the experiment; kept at 0 with medium confidence following the more conservative candidate.
B1 scored 0 (single measure = head twitch count) per rubric (1 measure = 0 points).
Sex confirmed female-only across all experiments.

post-judge trim: removed acute-toxicity (LD50 range-finding) doses from Psilocin / Pholiotina / Psilocybe dosing[] entries — these are not behavioural treatment doses. Original list included 180-450 mg/kg, explicitly labelled 'acute toxicity' in the paper's evidence.
